newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares edge higher on cautious buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares edge higher on cautious buying.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares edged higher on Thursday on cautious buying with most investors waiting for a clear trend to emerge before returning to the market, brokers said.
Trading volume was relatively thin on Thursday as investors were awaiting fresh news, including the announcement of more 1997 interim results, brokers said.
The B index closed up 0.477 points or 0.64 percent to 74.999 points on volume of 14.739 million shares worth $5.002 million.
"No one is trading actively," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "Investors don't want to risk their money because no clear market trend has emerged."
Interim results, which companies are required to report before the end of August, might help provide some direction to the market, brokers said.

Clothing-maker Shanghai Kaikai Industrial Co Ltd on Thursday said its net profit for the first half of 1997 rose 12 percent year-on-year to 34.593 million yuan, but the results had little impact on trading, brokers said.
Kaikai closed up $0.004 or 1.12 percent to $0.362 following a suspension from morning trading for the results announcement.

Some foreign investors were looking towards a major Communist Party meeting in September or October, which would chart China's future development, to provide fresh direction to the market, brokers said said.
"There won't be much news, positive or negative, before October," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm in Shanghai.
Of 45 B shares, 38 traded with 20 up, 12 down and six flat.
Penmaker Shanghai Hero Co was the top B share gainer on institutional buying, rising $0.022 or 6.08 percent to $0.384.

Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co was the most actively traded on institutional cross-trading amid mixed views about the company's prospects. It closed up $0.014 or 3.48 percent to $0.416 on volume of around 3.3 million shares.
Domestic currency A shares fell sharply due to weak market sentiment after positive results and other recent good news failed to lift the market, brokers said.
The A index fell 26.691 points or 2.13 percent to 1,227.928 points on volume of 310.212 million shares worth 3.780 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index lost 79.529 points or 2.08 percent to 3,741.811 points.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co was the biggest A share loser on expectations of poor results, plunging 0.57 yuan or 9.91 percent to 5.18 yuan.
A shares were likely to fall further on Friday, while B shares would trade in a narrow range of 73 to 77 points, brokers said.
